nodes.text: Let $n_k$ be minimal such that if $n_k$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ are in general position then there exists a subset of $k$ points such that all $\binom{k}{3}$ triples determine circles of different radii. Determine $n_k$.

#827 : [Er75h] [Er78c] [Er92e] geometry In [Er75h] Erdős asks whether $n_k$ exists. In [Er78c] he gave a simple argument which proves that it does, and in fact\[n_k \leq k+2\binom{k-1}{2}\binom{k-1}{3},\]but this argument is incorrect, as explained by Martinez and Roldán-Pensado [MaRo15] . Martinez and Roldán-Pensado give a corrected argument that proves $n_k\ll k^9$. A simple probabilistic argument, given in the comments by FlaredRain, improves this to $n_k\ll k^5$.
